key_insight: A single quantum run can recover multiple nuclear shell-model eigenstates at once by combining SSVQE with an adaptive, symmetry-preserving ansatz.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the need for repeated excited-state solves and offers a scalable quantum pathway for high-dimensional many-body nuclear structure calculations.
method: Map the fermionic shell-model Hamiltonian to qubits using the Jordan-Wigner transformation.
Use ADAPT-SSVQE with a single/double-excitation operator pool to optimize a weighted sum of energies.
Target a fixed MJ subspace and enforce orthogonality among simultaneously computed states.
evidence_signal: In simulation, the method extracted five states for two nucleons and ten states for three nucleons in a j=9/2 orbital using a 10-qubit active space, matching exact diagonalization with spectroscopic accuracy.
watch_item: The approach was validated in simulation on a small active space, so hardware noise, circuit depth, and scaling to larger shell-model spaces remain key implementation concerns.
paper_title: Full-Spectrum Quantum Simulation for the Nuclear Shell Model
